question: A 29-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of a swollen right knee. Over the past several weeks, he has had similar episodes affecting the right knee and sometimes also the left elbow, in which the swelling lasted an average of 5 days. He has a history of a rash that subsided 2 months ago. He lives in Connecticut with his wife and works as a landscaper. His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 110/75 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a tender and warm right knee; range of motion is limited by pain. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. His hematocrit is 44%, leukocyte count is 10,300/mm3, and platelet count is 145,000/mm3. Serum electrolyte concentrations are within normal limits. Arthrocentesis is performed and the synovial fluid is cloudy. Gram stain is negative. Analysis of the synovial fluid shows a leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3 and 80% neutrophils. Serologic testing confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "29-year-old man with swollen right knee" -> "history of similar episodes" -> "episodes lasted about 5 days" -> "previous rash 2 months ago" -> "lives in Connecticut" -> "works as a landscaper" -> "cloudy synovial fluid" -> "high leukocyte count of 70,000/mm3" -> " -> 80%

CHAIN: "29-year-old man with swollen right knee" -> "episodes of swelling in joints" -> "previous rash suggests possible infection" -> "lives in area endemic for Lyme disease" -> "cloudy synovial fluid" -> "high leukocyte count with neutrophils" -> "negative Gram stain indicates non-bacterial infection" -> "serologic testing confirms diagnosis" -> "most likely cause is Borrelia burgdorferi" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Swollen right knee in young man" -> "history of joint swelling episodes" -> "rash subsided 2 months ago" -> "cloudy synovial fluid with high leukocyte count" -> " -> 80%
CHAIN: "Young man with joint swelling" -> "episodes of swelling in knee and elbow" -> "rash history suggests possible infection" -> "cloudy synovial fluid with high leukocyte count" -> " -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent swollen joints (right knee and left elbow), a history of rash, and the location of residence in Connecticut, strongly suggest Lyme disease, which is caused by Borrelia burgdorferi. The synovial fluid analysis showing a high leukocyte count with a predominance of neutrophils further supports an inflammatory process consistent with Lyme arthritis. Other options like osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis are less likely given the acute nature of the swelling and the patient's age. Neisseria gonorrhoeae is also less likely due to the negative Gram stain and the patient's history. Campylobacter jejuni is not typically associated with joint swelling. Therefore, the most likely cause of the patient's symptoms is Borrelia burgdorferi.
